page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.1-16 is a flexible virtual machine instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core of an Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor running at a base clock speed of 3.9 GHz, utilizing two hardware threads per core. The instance is paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 8.0 GB per core.

The instance contains no integrated local NVMe or SSD storage, necessitating network-attached block volumes for persistent data retention and operating system hosting. Furthermore, it operates without hardware accelerators, featuring zero discrete GPUs. Network provisioning includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for direct external interface capabilities.

With an elevated memory-to-core ratio of 8 GB per vCPU, VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.1-16 offers strong resource density for memory-bound tasks without requiring high core counts. This footprint makes the instance cost-efficient for small-scale caching layers, light in-memory datastores, background worker nodes, and web microservices requiring moderate working sets rather than intensive multi-threaded processing.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.1-16 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor operating at 3.9 GHz. The configuration allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs across 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, coupled with 16.0 GB of system memory. This yields a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per virtual core. The server includes no onboard local storage, depending on remote block storage solutions for disk operations, and contains zero GPUs. One complimentary public IPv4 address is provided for network ingress and egress. Because the memory allocation is comparatively high for a dual-thread single-core profile, the instance provides cost efficiency for memory-sensitive services that do not require wide parallel compute. It is suited for in-memory caches, small transactional databases, application backend services, and lightweight container hosts.
